title: MCP for Dummies
tagline: AI that actually does things, not just talks.
description: A 60-card guided run through the protocol that connects AI to real tools and data.

modules.title: What MCP Really Is
modules.summary: The core idea behind the universal AI adapter.

cards.content: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It’s the open standard that lets any AI model plug straight into your data, tools, and systems.
Think of it as USB-C for AI. One clean connector instead of a drawer full of mismatched cables.
Anthropic open-sourced MCP in late 2024 to end the chaos of custom integrations between AI and everything else.
It turns chatty models into real agents that can fetch live files, call APIs, or update records safely.
No more training-data-only limits. MCP gives AI fresh context from the real world on demand.
Developers write one MCP server. Every compatible AI can use it instantly.
The protocol runs on simple JSON-RPC calls, so it’s fast, reliable, and easy to secure.
MCP isn’t another AI model. It’s the plumbing that makes every model more useful.
It standardizes how AI asks for context, uses tools, and gets results back without drama.
If you remember one thing: MCP is the missing piece that finally makes AI act like a true teammate.

modules.title: The Integration Headache
modules.summary: Why AI was stuck before MCP arrived.

cards.content: Every AI vendor used its own weird way to reach your data. Developers rebuilt the same bridge over and over.
Change one database schema and every AI integration broke at once.
Security teams hated it. Custom code meant custom attack surfaces everywhere.
Models hallucinated because they had zero access to your latest numbers or files.
Agents dreamed of booking flights or creating tickets, but the plumbing was never there.
Companies wasted months wiring each new tool instead of shipping real features.
Tool calling felt like a hack. It worked until it didn’t.
Different models spoke different languages to the same APIs. Pure friction.
The dream of agentic AI stayed just a dream without a shared standard.
MCP killed that headache in one stroke by giving everyone the same plug.

modules.title: How MCP Works
modules.summary: The protocol that makes connections click.

cards.content: MCP uses a simple client-server model. Your app runs an MCP server that exposes tools and data.
The AI client discovers what the server offers and asks for exactly what it needs.
Everything travels as structured JSON-RPC messages, so there’s no guesswork.
The AI decides which tool to call, sends a clean request, and gets a clean response.
Human-in-the-loop is baked in. You can approve big actions before they fire.
Servers can stream results in real time, so the AI isn’t waiting around.
Context is scoped. The AI only sees what you explicitly allow.
It works locally or in the cloud. Your laptop files or your enterprise database, same protocol.
The AI keeps a conversation state across multiple tool calls, chaining actions naturally.
One protocol, endless possibilities. That’s the mechanical beauty of MCP.

modules.title: Clients, Servers & Tools
modules.summary: The pieces that make MCP tick.

cards.content: MCP server: the lightweight app you build to expose your tools, files, or APIs.
MCP client: the part inside the AI that talks to any server using the standard.
Tools are functions the server registers. The AI can call them like built-in skills.
Context sources let the AI read specific files, database rows, or search results on demand.
Prompt templates live on the server so the AI always gets consistent instructions.
Permissions are declared up front. The AI knows exactly what it can and cannot touch.
Discovery happens automatically. The AI asks the server what’s available.
Sessions keep everything stateful across back-and-forth tool calls.
Reference implementations from Anthropic make spinning up a server stupidly easy.
The whole stack stays lightweight so you’re not dragging in a heavyweight framework.

modules.title: MCP in Action
modules.summary: Where it’s already powering real AI agents.

cards.content: A developer asks Claude to fix a bug. MCP server hands over the exact repo files and runs the fix locally.
An AI agent books your next flight by talking to your calendar and airline APIs through one MCP server.
Sales teams let AI pull live CRM data, draft emails, and log everything without copy-paste hell.
Data analysts query fresh warehouse numbers in natural language while the MCP server keeps everything secure.
Code editors use MCP to let AI edit your actual project files with full context and undo safety.
Support bots create Jira tickets, update customer records, and confirm with you before sending.
Personal AI assistants manage your email, schedule meetings, and attach the right docs on the fly.
Enterprise teams connect the same MCP server to Claude, GPT, or any future model without extra work.
Local MCP servers on your laptop give AI safe access to private notes without sending data to the cloud.
The pattern is clear: MCP turns “it can explain” into “it can execute.”

modules.title: Using MCP Well
modules.summary: How to turn the protocol into real leverage.

cards.content: Start small. Expose one tool or folder first so you can test safely.
Always declare tight permissions. The AI should only touch what it needs.
Add human approval steps for any action that costs money or changes data.
Keep your MCP server lightweight and versioned so updates don’t break existing AI clients.
Use clear tool names and descriptions. The AI picks better when it understands intent.
Combine MCP with your favorite AI model and watch it go from thinker to doer in seconds.
Monitor logs. You’ll spot exactly which tools the AI uses most and refine them fast.
Share your MCP server internally. One server can power every team’s AI workflows.
Iterate on the AI’s prompts inside the server so responses stay on-brand and accurate.
The real win isn’t replacing people. It’s giving every AI the context and tools to multiply what you can do.
